note: The weekly loop's first challengers, from the research (17 Nov 2026): what the research was unsure of, ranked, alternating first-second and look tests.

candidates.test: 45-55 s Shorts against the 60-80 s champion
candidates.why: the niche's median is 65 s, but channel #1 learned shorter Shorts hold better; untested here

candidates.test: satellite terrain maps (Natural Earth relief) instead of flat political maps
candidates.why: the biggest small-channel hit (Chile, 10.6M) and Map & Myth use it; the owner chose flat maps first

candidates.test: the title and the first line name the strange thing you can see on the map (a thin finger, a tiny triangle, a straight line, a strip, a wall) before the place's name, e.g. 'Why does Afghanistan have a thin finger reaching China?', against the champion's 'Place + fact. Why?' title
candidates.why: Odd Atlas (5.25K subscribers, median 56.7K views a Short over 53 Shorts in 60 days, scan of 17 Nov): 9 of its 15 most-watched titles name a visible shape (triangle 554K, strip 540K and 274K, finger 277K, wall 220K, straight lines 128K, shaped like a river 138K, ruler 114K, slice 103K). Our titles name the place and a fact ('Greenland belongs to Denmark. Why?' 1,213 views; 'Hormuz shuts for a week' 160). No stayed-to-watch data of ours yet, so it is placed after the claim-hook test.

candidates.test: the camera moves from frame 0: the first beat opens on a push-in (globe or region down to the named place, the place's name writing on large) that starts on the first frame, instead of opening on a held medium shot with the first push-in on the line's last words
candidates.why: All 5 reference Shorts we have shot sheets for (Chile 10.6M, Roll Down a Hill 2.8M, One Country 2.95M, Louisiana, Caspian 2.1M) open with motion 2 and a push-in or tipping move in the first 3-5 s with no text on screen; our Suez Short (18 Nov) holds a medium shot of Egypt with a small 'SUEZ CANAL' label until the word 'closed' (~4 s). No stayed-to-watch data of ours yet (first Short published 18 Nov), so it waits behind the higher-ranked first-second tests.

candidates.test: narration at the recipe's stated pace, about 185 words a minute (bm_george's speed lowered for the challenger side so a 60-80 s Short carries about 185-245 words), against the champion as rendered now, 203-226 words a minute
candidates.why: All five reference Shorts speak slower than our slowest: 150, 174, 185, 189 and 194 wpm (median 185; Louisiana 18.7M, Chile 10.6M, One Country 2.95M, Roll Down a Hill 2.77M, Caspian 2.09M; research/sheets word counts over their length). Our last 8 Shorts: 203-226 wpm, median about 217 (render.json words over duration_sec), about 17% faster, while the recipe itself says about 185. If the challenger loses, the recipe's pace line should be corrected to what the champion actually speaks.

candidates.test: when a beat's change is a map changing (pieces joining, a border moving, a place moving or growing), the shapes morph or slide from the old state into the new one on the spoken word, as one continuous move, instead of a cut or match to a new shot; at least two such morph beats per Short, against the champion's cut/match transitions
candidates.why: Our last three Shorts (v-20261123-11, v-20261124-11, v-20261124-12) use 18 cuts and 17 match transitions and no morphs; their pace already matches the references (5.4-6.0 s a beat against 4.3-7.9 s, median 5.9, in the five sheets), so the gap is in how the picture changes, not how often. Two of the five reference sheets morph shapes (BmNSUb8HxCA twice, 7iZflr3qD-4 once), and this week's biggest outlier in the scan is built on it: Geo Cartovia's 'How Italy Became One Country, From 7 Pieces to 1' (232K views on 782 subscribers, 297x) and its Spain version (95K, 121x), whose pieces snap together on screen. Lower confidence than geo-pace-185: two sheets and one channel.

candidates.test: a DAY 1...7 counter on screen for what-if stories
candidates.why: WorldShift's 2.95M hit is built on it

candidates.test: a place-and-resources story ('why is a desert country rich?')
candidates.why: part of the owner's concept; families.json ranks it 0.33x on 43 Shorts, so it is tested before it is relied on

candidates.test: the second beat (the first fact line, about 5 to 7 s) opens close on the named place and pulls out as its figure lands on the spoken number, against the champion's medium map shot with the figure label already in frame
candidates.why: Picture tally of 23 Nov: in all 5 Shorts with drop points the steepest fall is the second beat, 15.3 to 23.9 points (average 18.1), and all 5 opened that beat on a medium map shot; map shots carrying a figure lost 15.4 points a drop (7 drops, 5 Shorts) against 9.3 for map shots without one (8 drops).

candidates.test: the explorer/atlas bed about 20 dB under the voice instead of about 31 dB, ducking unchanged, effects unchanged
candidates.why: Our last 8 Shorts sit 30.4-31.7 dB music-under-voice (render.json audio), so the bed is close to inaudible on a phone. The two measured references split: Map & Myth's Chile (10.6M) at 16 dB, WorldShift's One Country (2.95M) at 39 dB (style-study/2026-11-18-references.md). Weak evidence, so last among the look tests.

candidates.test: the loop beat goes straight from the payoff back into the first line, with no 'X or Y: which should we map next? Tell me in the comments' question, against the champion's comment question before the loop
candidates.why: Every Short with drop points loses viewers on the comment question in its last beat: 21.0% at 62.4 s (One passport), 13.2% + 5.7% (Sahara), 6.1% + 8.4% (English cities), 9.3% (Tristan), 9.1% (Hormuz), 7.9% (Greenland), 5.9% (Dinorwig). Some of that is the natural end, so it is a test, not a lesson: the reference Shorts loop without asking.

candidates.test: On a scene-layout cover (script.thumbnail, layout 'scene'), when the big words don't name the place (5 of our last 8 covers: 'Why is it Danish?', 'Who lives here?', 'How did it grow?', 'What is it stopping?', 'Why the hole?'), draw thumbnail.tag (already filled in every script: 'Australia', 'Lesotho', 'Russia') as a large label under the words. Today Thumbnail.tsx draws tag only inside the figure card, so a scene cover without a figure shows no name (the Dingo Fence and Africa covers have none). Behind a flag on half the Shorts.
candidates.why: More taps from search and the channel page (about 4% of our views); no effect on the feed.

history.from: owner note 19 Nov on v-20261119-02: 'test both' (flag vs colour)

history.test: a claim whose answer waits for the end, instead of the question as the first line
history.why: 'Only one country here rolls like a real wheel' (2.7M) opened on a claim | research 2026-11-23, our own first lines: the one Short that opens on a contradiction you can see on the map ('Greenland sits next to Canada, not Europe, yet it belongs to Denmark. Why?') has the best average viewed (74.7%, 1,224 views); plain 'Why did…' / 'What if…' openers sit at 48% (Dinorwig) and 55% (Suez). Three Shorts with Analytics only, so the order is unchanged.
